gloss: self-sufficiency; being content with what one has

definitions.gloss: self-sufficiency; meeting one's own needs; being content with what one has
definitions.explanation: Supplying one's own needs or being satisfied with what one already has — without seeking more from outside. Most commonly seen in the four-character compound {自給自足|じきゅうじそく} (self-sufficiency).

examples.japanese: {自給|じきゅう}{自足|じそく}の{生活|せいかつ}。
{小|ちい}さな{畑|はたけ}で{野菜|やさい}を{自足|じそく}している。
examples.english: We supply our own vegetables from a small field.

examples.japanese: {現代|げんだい}の{都市|とし}{生活|せいかつ}では、{食料|しょくりょう}を{自足|じそく}することはほぼ{不可能|ふかのう}だ。
examples.english: In modern urban life, it is nearly impossible to be self-sufficient in food.

examples.japanese: {彼|かれ}らは{山|やま}の{中|なか}で、{電気|でんき}も{水道|すいどう}も{使|つか}わずに{自足|じそく}の{暮|く}らしを{続|つづ}けている。
examples.english: In the mountains, they continue a self-sufficient life without using electricity or running water.

notes:
Composed of {自|じ} (self) and {足|そく} (be sufficient, suffice). Refers to meeting one's own needs or being satisfied with what one has. In modern Japanese, {自足|じそく} rarely appears on its own — it is most commonly encountered as part of the four-character idiom {自給自足|じきゅうじそく} (self-sufficiency: producing and consuming one's own goods).

USAGE:
- As a noun: {自足|じそく}の{生活|せいかつ} (a self-sufficient life)
- As a suru-verb: {野菜|やさい}を{自足|じそく}する (to supply one's own vegetables)
- Often combined: {自給|じきゅう}{自足|じそく} (the standard idiomatic form)

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {自給|じきゅう}{自足|じそく}: self-sufficiency (idiomatic four-character compound)
- {自足|じそく}の{生活|せいかつ}: a self-sufficient life
- {自足|じそく}できない: cannot supply one's own / cannot be satisfied
- {食料|しょくりょう}を{自足|じそく}する: to meet one's own food needs

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {自給|じきゅう}: self-supply — the more common half of {自給自足|じきゅうじそく}; emphasizes production
- {独立|どくりつ}: independence — broader; includes political and emotional independence
- {自立|じりつ}: independence, standing on one's own — focuses on personal autonomy rather than supplying one's needs
- {満足|まんぞく}: satisfaction, contentment — emphasizes feeling, not supply
